title: Sales is more than selling
caption: Selling early pays before the revenue does.

board.label: Market insight, trust and a repeatable process all lead to increased trust.

market-insight.label: Market insight
market-insight.line: Every customer talk is market research.

trust.label: Trust
trust.line: An early deal, even a small one, is proof.

repeatable-process.label: Repeatable process
repeatable-process.line: The steps that work, written down for your first sales hire.

outcome.label: Increase trust
outcome.line: A company others dare to bet on.

your-guess-of-the-customer-is-wrong.header: Your guess of the customer is wrong
your-guess-of-the-customer-is-wrong.description: A founder's initial model of users is always inaccurate, even if the founder is one of them; direct contact is what corrects it.[1]

graham-do-things-that-dont-scale.title: Graham, Do Things that Don't Scale

investors-read-the-team.description: Among 885 venture capitalists the management team was the most-cited important factor (95%), ahead of product and market. That a signed letter of intent or a full pipeline raises trust is an inference: no study tests them directly.[1]

gompers-how-vcs-decide.title: Gompers, Gornall, Kaplan and Strebulaev, How Do Venture Capitalists Make Decisions?

scale-after-you-find-the-process.header: Scale after you find the process
scale-after-you-find-the-process.description: Premature scaling of sales and marketing is the leading cause of cash loss in a startup; scale after the founders have found a repeatable sales model.[1]

blank-marketing-problem.title: Blank, It Must Be A Marketing Problem

market-insight.title: Market insight
market-insight.keywords: wrong buyer, build already paid for, price of skipping early sales
market-insight.script: The first note: market insight. Look at your offer. Suppose it is aimed at the wrong buyer. You will not see that on the board. You will see it after the build is paid for. The money is gone, and the offer still has to change. That is the price of skipping early sales.

trust.title: Trust
trust.keywords: customers and investors, an early deal, paid attention or money, faith
trust.script: The second note: trust. Customers and investors both trust a company that has already sold something. An early deal, even a small one, says that someone paid attention, or paid money. A company with nothing sold asks them to take it on faith.

repeatable-process.title: Repeatable process
repeatable-process.keywords: which steps work, write it down, first sales hire
repeatable-process.script: The third note: a repeatable process. When you sell yourself, you see which steps work, and in which order. Write that down. It becomes the process you can later hand to a first sales hire, instead of handing over a hope.

converge-on-trust.title: Converge on trust
converge-on-trust.keywords: three notes, three arrows, a company others dare to bet on
converge-on-trust.script: Three notes, three arrows, one place they end. A company others dare to bet on. That is what early selling builds, long before it builds revenue.
